A1.justification: Both PDFs describe QUAD for continual visual question answering, despite the changed title. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching.

before.justification: v1 reports original VQAv2 and NExT-QA experiments, component ablations, memory-size sensitivity, question-selection comparisons, and task-retention matrices.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds pretrained-model evaluations, attention-drift measurements, a loss-weight sensitivity study, and a controlled answer-space experiment.

M1.justification: Equation 1 changes LPlasticity + λLStability to (1 − λ)LPlasticity + λLStability. At the retained λ = 0.5, this changes the relative weighting. Question selection, soft-label replay, and attention distillation remain; LPL/LAtt become LQR/LACD. The PDFs do not establish whether the objective revision reflects rerun experiments.

E1.justification: Both versions use VQAv2 and NExT-QA with the same linguistic tasks, object groups, and novel-composition coverage. The added architecture evaluations and controlled counting/action/color experiment reuse existing task coverage; their changes concern configurations and evaluation procedures.

E2.justification: v2 substantially broadens evaluated comparators through GaB-classifier and GaB-clustering in the BLIP-2 comparison (Table 5), and CL-MoE in the LLaVA-7B comparison (Table 6). The original EWC, MAS, ER, DER, VS, VQACL, and attention-distillation comparisons remain.

E3.justification: v2 adds BLIP-2 and LLaVA-7B configurations, entropy-difference and attention-coherence measurements, and a λ sweep. Section 14 introduces a controlled three-task sequence with fixed answer vocabularies and ten evaluation questions per task. The original feature extraction, T5 training budget, and object-independent cross-validation remain.

E4.justification: New analyses test whether QUAD preserves attention distributions (Section 10, Figures 7–8), how performance depends on λ (Section 12, Figure 9), and whether replay prevents answer-space drift (Section 14, Figure 2). Existing component, memory-size, question-selection, and plasticity/stability analyses are retained.

E5.justification: The existing five-fold object-independent cross-validation is unchanged. Neither version provides seed-based variability, confidence intervals, or significance tests; the added tables and plots continue reporting point estimates.

E6.justification: Tables 1–4 and the original task-retention matrices retain their numerical results. New Table 5 reports BLIP-2 QUAD AP 50.27 and forgetting 1.04, versus VQACL 49.80 and 1.18. Table 6 reports LLaVA-7B QUAD AP 44.16, below CL-MoE's 52.96. New drift measurements, confusion matrices, and λ results substantially expand the reported evidence.

T1.justification: v2 adds a formal comparison of L1 and cross-entropy attention alignment, including gradient expressions in Section 9, and mathematical definitions of the new drift measurements in Section 10. This extends the mathematical treatment beyond v1's method objectives and storage-complexity analysis. The new gradient in Equation 11 is not justified by Equation 10 as written.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain question-only rehearsal and attention-consistency distillation for memory-efficient continual VQA. The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the claims of reduced visual-data storage and strong benchmark performance. Recasting QUAD as a replay framework does not materially change those contributions.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive interpretations of attention-gradient behavior, measured attention drift, the optimal stability/plasticity balance, and transfer to pretrained architectures. Section 13 additionally positions CL-MoE's stronger performance outside the question-only storage constraint. These interpretations substantially extend v1, while Section 8's visual-reasoning and privacy limitations remain essentially unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 specifies the new diagnostic's task order, answer vocabularies, and ten questions per task, and reports 5,000-item buffers for the pretrained-model comparisons. Original implementation settings, computational discussion, and code-access information remain. Detailed fine-tuning instructions for the added backbones are not supplied.

R1.justification: v2 adds literature on pretrained VLMs, GaB, CL-MoE, recency bias, and attention alignment. It explicitly contrasts QUAD with generated replay and exemplar-based expert methods. These extend the research context while retaining the original positioning around question-only memory for continual VQA.

P1.justification: The title changes to 'Ask and Remember,' and substantial portions of the abstract, introduction, related work, method explanation, and analysis prose are rewritten. Loss terminology changes throughout the main paper, and the appendix gains several organized sections while retaining and renumbering earlier material.

P2.justification: v2 adds the answer-space confusion matrices, two attention-drift heatmaps, a λ plot, and two architecture-comparison tables. The method overview is visually revised. Original plots and dataset tables are retained with updated labels, numbering, and placement, producing a substantial expansion of the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: The pretrained-model comparisons and new sensitivity studies usefully broaden validation. However, the added attention analysis claims higher coherence despite Figure 8 showing final-row averages of 0.325 for QUAD versus 0.328 for both baselines. Section 13 also claims improvement across all LLaVA question types although Table 6 shows commonsense declining from VQACL's 63.00 to 62.15. Together with the unsupported gradient expression, these new reliability problems make the net benefit of the expanded evidence uncertain.
